353317.title: Hypergraphic planted clique detection conjecture
353317.statement:
Let $H$ be an order-$K$ hypergraph in the HPC detection problem, with null distribution $H_0:H\sim\mathcal{H}_K(p,1/2)$ and planted-clique alternative $H_1:H\sim\mathcal{H}_K(p,1/2,\kappa_p)$, where $\{\kappa_p\}$ satisfies

$$
\limsup_{p\to\infty}\frac{\log\kappa_p}{\log\sqrt{p}}\leq 1-\tau.
$$

A polynomial-time test is a sequence $\{\varphi_p\}$ with $\varphi_p:H\mapsto\{0,1\}$. **HPC conjecture.** For every sequence of polynomial-time tests $\{\varphi_p\}$,

$$
\liminf_{p\to\infty}\mathbb{P}_{H_0}\bigl(\varphi_p(H)=1\bigr)+\mathbb{P}_{H_1}\bigl(\varphi_p(H)=0\bigr)\geq\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Thus, when the planted clique size is below the stated threshold, no polynomial-time test can reliably distinguish the null hypergraph from the hypergraph with a planted clique. This computational hardness conjecture is used to derive computational limits for degree-corrected tensor block models; its resolution status is not specified in the source.

355057.title: Spectral inequality conjecture for power-growth Schrödinger operators with ball-containing sensor sets
355057.statement:
Let $\tau>0$ and let $\function{P}_\tau$ denote the spectral projector associated with $-Delta+|x|^\tau$. Suppose that $omega\five subset\real^d$ is measurable and that, for some $delta\five in(0,1/2)$ and $alpha\five geq0$, every intersection $omega\five cap(k+(-1/2,1/2)^d)$, $k\five in\real^d$, contains a ball of radius $delta^{1+|k|^alpha}$. **Power-growth spectral inequality conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$, depending only on $tau$, $delta$, $alpha$, and $d$, such that for all $lambda\five geq1$ and all $f\five in\function{Ran}P_lambda(-Delta+|x|^tau)$,

$$
\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)}left(\frac1{\delta}\right)^{C\cdot\lambda^{\frac{\alpha}{\tau}+\frac12}}\|f\|_{L^2(\omega)}.
$$

This was proposed as a partial improvement of the paper's spectral inequality; the conjecture was later confirmed by Alphonse and the second author. The condition is intended to replace the stronger regularity assumption that every unit-cube intersection contains a ball, while retaining an explicit dependence on the spectral parameter.

357362.title: QTC2 plane partitions enumeration conjecture
357362.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a plane partition inside an $(a,a,c)$-box. It is **quasi transpose complementary of second kind** (QTC2) if it is transpose complementary except along the diagonal, namely

$$
\pi_{i,j}+\pi_{a+1-j,a+1-i}=c
$$

for all $1\leq i,j\leq a$ with $i\neq j$. Let $\operatorname{qtcpp}_2(a,c)$ denote the number of QTC2 plane partitions, and let $p_a(c)$ be a polynomial in $\mathbb{Q}[c]$. **QTC2 enumeration conjecture.** For $a\geq2$,

$$
\operatorname{qtcpp}_2\left(a,c-\frac{a}{2}\right)=\begin{cases}
c\binom{c+\frac{a}{2}-1}{a-1}p_a(c)&a\text{ is even},\\
\binom{c+\frac{a}{2}-1}{a-1}p_a(c)&a\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

Here $p_a(c)$ is irreducible and even, and the common denominator of its coefficients is a product of “small primes”. The formula was proposed from computer experiments and remains unproved.

358445.title: Generic lens spaces are spectrally unique
358445.statement:
For positive integers $n$ and $q$, let $\mathfrak L(n,q)$ be the isometry classes of $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens spaces with fundamental group of order $q$. Define the spectrally unique subset

$$
\mathfrak L^{\bullet}(n,q)=\\{L\in\mathfrak L(n,q):\operatorname{Spec}(L)\neq\operatorname{Spec}(L')\quad\forall L'\neq L\text{ in }\mathfrak L(n,q)\\}.
$$

For $x>0$, set

$$
\mathcal U_n(x)=\frac{\sum_{q\leq x}\\#\mathfrak L^{\bullet}(n,q)}{\sum_{q\leq x}\\#\mathfrak L(n,q)}.
$$

**Generic lens-space spectral uniqueness conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{x\to\infty}\mathcal U_n(x)=1
$$

for all $n\in\mathbb N$. This is a proposed extension of Wolpert's generic spectral-uniqueness results for Riemann surfaces and flat tori. Since the space of lens spaces has no natural topology, the conjecture uses density among spaces whose fundamental-group order is at most $x$; the source mentions numerical evidence but does not state a proof.

359392.title: The projective-index classification conjecture for finite linear group actions on \(\mathbb{C}^2\)
359392.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group with a linear action on $\mathbb{C}^2$. Its **projective indices** $\tau_P^G$ and associated canonical group are among the following possibilities: $\{(0,0)\}$ for a cyclic group; $\{(0,0),(1,1),(3,3),\ldots,(m^*,m^*)\}$ for a binary dihedral group of order $4m$; $\{(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(5,5)\}$ for a binary tetrahedral group; $\{(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(5,5),(7,7),(11,11)\}$ for a binary octahedral group; or $\{(p,p):p=0,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,13,14,17,19,23,29\}$ for a binary icosahedral group.

**Projective-index classification conjecture.** Every finite group with a linear action on $\mathbb{C}^2$ has one of these five projective-index sets and associated canonical groups.

The paper explains that the list of canonical groups is known, and that the remaining issue is excluding further projective indices $(p,p)$ with $p>100$, beyond the range computed. Thus the classification is supported by computation but is not established in full.

361045.title: Extremal image-size conjecture for pop-stack operators on type A Cambrian lattices
361045.statement:
Let $A_n$ be the type-$A_n$ Coxeter system, and let $c$ be any Coxeter element of $A_n$. Write $c^{\to}=s_1s_2\cdots s_n$ for the linear Coxeter element and let $c^{\times}$ be a bipartite Coxeter element. For a Coxeter element $d$, let $\mathrm{Camb}_d$ denote the corresponding Cambrian lattice and let $\mathrm{pop}^{\downarrow}_{\mathrm{Camb}_d}$ be its pop-stack operator.

**Extremal image-size conjecture.** For every Coxeter element $c$ of $A_n$, we have

$$
\left|\mathrm{pop}^{\downarrow}_{\mathrm{Camb}_{c^\to}}(\mathrm{Camb}_{c^\to})\right|\leq\left|\mathrm{pop}^{\downarrow}_{\mathrm{Camb}_{c}}(\mathrm{Camb}_{c})\right|\leq\left|\mathrm{pop}^{\downarrow}_{\mathrm{Camb}_{c^\times}}(\mathrm{Camb}_{c^\times})\right|.
$$

The conjecture formalizes numerical evidence that the linear and bipartite Coxeter elements are extremal for the sizes of the images of pop-stack operators. The first inequality is consistent with the known comparison between the linear and bipartite cases, while the general assertion remains open.

362660.title: Gaussoid axioms suffice for CI implication in singly constrained Gaussian DAG models
362660.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a directed acyclic graph (DAG), and let $i \perp\!\!\!\perp j \mid K$ be a conditional independence statement such that $i \not\perp_{\mathcal{G}} j \mid K$. Denote by $\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{G}, i \perp\!\!\!\perp j\mid K}$ the Gaussian model associated with $\mathcal{G}$ together with this additional conditional independence statement. Let $\operatorname{global}(\mathcal{G})$ be the set of global Markov conditional independence statements of $\mathcal{G}$.

**Gaussoid-axioms sufficiency conjecture.** If $a \perp\!\!\!\perp b \mid C$ holds for every covariance matrix $\Sigma \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{G}, i \perp\!\!\!\perp j\mid K}$, then $a \perp\!\!\!\perp b \mid C$ is implied by applying the gaussoid axioms to

$$
\operatorname{global}(\mathcal{G}) \cup \{i \perp\!\!\!\perp j \mid K\}.
$$

The conjecture is verified in the paper for models involving four random variables, but its validity for arbitrary numbers of variables remains open.

364539.title: Almost equitable factorization conjecture with controlled parity defects
364539.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_k$ be nonnegative real numbers satisfying

$$
\varepsilon_1+\cdots+\varepsilon_k=1,
$$

and let $G$ be a graph. An **edge-decomposition into factors** is a decomposition of $E(G)$ into the edge sets of factors $G_1,\ldots,G_k$. For each vertex $v$, let $j_v$ denote an index whose factor has odd degree at $v$, when such an index exists.

**Almost equitable factorization conjecture.** The graph $G$ can be edge-decomposed into factors $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ such that, for every $v\in V(G)$,

$$
\left|d_{G_i}(v)-\varepsilon_i d_G(v)\right|<2\qquad(1\le i\le k),
$$

and at most one factor has odd degree at $v$. In particular, no such index exists when $d_G(v)$ is even. Furthermore, if $G$ is odd-$\lceil 1/\varepsilon_1\rceil$-edge-connected, then $j_v=1$ for every odd-degree vertex $v$.

The source says that the conjecture is proved when almost all proportions are equal, except possibly $\varepsilon_1$, and that a weaker version with upper bound $6$ is confirmed. The full statement remains open.

364648.title: Higher-dimensional Neumann monotonicity conjecture
364648.statement:
Let $C(\Theta)$ be the geodesic ball of radius $\Theta$ in the constant-curvature model, and let $\mu_k(\Theta)$ denote its $k^{\text{th}}$ Neumann eigenvalue. At $\Theta=0$, let $\mu_k(\mathbb{B}^n)$ denote the corresponding eigenvalue of the Euclidean ball $\mathbb{B}^n\subset\mathbb{R}^n$.

**Higher-dimensional Neumann monotonicity conjecture.** The function

$$
\Theta \mapsto \begin{cases} \mu_k(\Theta)\,\sinh^2(\Theta), & \Theta\in(-\infty,0), \\ \mu_k(\mathbb{B}^n), & \Theta=0, \\ \mu_k(\Theta)\,\sin^2(\Theta), & \Theta\in(0,\pi/2), \end{cases}
$$

decreases strictly from $\infty$ to $0$, for all $k\geq2$ and $n\geq3$.

The claim is supported by numerical evidence, but the proof used for the Dirichlet spectrum does not transfer readily to the Neumann case. The corresponding statement in dimension $n=2$ was proved by Langford and Laugesen.

365286.title: The Hamiltonian-path strengthening of Rafla's conjecture
365286.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph, let $\mathcal{D}$ be a simple drawing of it on $n\ge 2$ vertices, and let $v$ and $w$ be distinct vertices of $\mathcal{D}$. A **crossing-free Hamiltonian path** is a path that visits every vertex exactly once, has no crossing edges, and whose end-vertices are $v$ and $w$. **Hamiltonian-path strengthening.** Every simple drawing $\mathcal{D}$ of $K_n$ on $n\ge 2$ vertices contains, for each pair of vertices $v \neq w$ in $\mathcal{D}$, a crossing-free Hamiltonian path with end-vertices $v$ and $w$.

The source states that this conjecture strengthens Rafla's Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture and that the implication between the two holds for the drawing classes considered there. It was confirmed for cylindrical and strongly c-monotone drawings, but the supplied text leaves the assertion open for arbitrary simple drawings.

365498.title: Sorting-order characterization conjecture for Stanley coefficients
365498.statement:
For a partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)$, let $E_\lambda^U$ be the set of $\lambda$-Escher tuples, let $\tau_\lambda:E_\lambda^U\to\mathbb{Q}^{\xi(\lambda)}$ be the core representation, and let $E_\lambda^U(\tau)$ be the subset whose core vector has sorting permutation $\tau$. Let $c_\lambda^U$ denote the Stanley coefficient. **Sorting-order characterization conjecture.** For every partition $\lambda$ there is a set of sorting orders

$$
T_\lambda=\{\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_{N(\lambda)}\},
$$

independent of $U$, such that

$$
c_\lambda^U=\#\bigl(E_\lambda^U(\tau_1)\cup\cdots\cup E_\lambda^U(\tau_N)\bigr).
$$

Thus $T_\lambda$ characterizes the Stanley coefficient $c_\lambda$. The claim is the formal version of the paper’s experimentally motivated assertion that Stanley coefficients are determined by sorting orders rather than by the numerical values of core coordinates; the source reports computational evidence but no resolution.

367518.title: The full Brouwer's Laplacian spectrum conjecture
367518.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges and Laplacian eigenvalues $\mu_1\geq\mu_2\geq\cdots\geq\mu_n$, and define

$$
s_k(G):=\sum_{i=1}^k\mu_i.
$$

For integers $k\in\{1,2,\cdots,n-1\}$, let $G_{k,r,s}$ be the graph of order $n=k+r+s$ consisting of a clique $K_k$ and two independent sets $\overline{K_r}$ and $\overline{K_s}$, with every vertex of $K_k$ adjacent to every vertex of $\overline{K_r}$, and with

$$
N(v_i)\subsetneq V(K_k),\qquad N(v_{i+1})\subseteq N(v_i)
$$

for $i=1,2,\cdots,s$ and $i=1,2,\cdots,s-1$, respectively. **The full Brouwer's conjecture.** For every such $k$,

$$
s_k(G)\leq m+\binom{k+1}{2},
$$

with equality if and only if $G\cong G_{k,r,s}$ for some $r\geq1$ and $s\geq0$. This is equivalent to requiring that equality holds exactly for threshold graphs with $n$ vertices and clique number $k+1$. The conjecture has been confirmed for graphs with at most $9$ vertices and for several values of $k$, but remains open in general.

370269.title: Baur's magnetic Faber–Krahn conjecture for higher eigenvalues
370269.statement:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^2$ be a bounded simply-connected planar domain with area $|\Omega|=1$, and let $n\in\mathbb N$. For a homogeneous magnetic field of strength $B\geq 0$, let $\lambda_n(\Omega,B)$ denote the $n$th eigenvalue of the shifted magnetic Laplacian with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Let $\mathbb D$ be the disk of unit area. **Baur's conjecture.** For all $B\geq 2\pi n$, 

$$
\lambda_n(\Omega,B)\geq\lambda_n(\mathbb D,B).
$$

This conjecture proposes that, above the threshold $2\pi n$, the unit-area disk minimizes the $n$th eigenvalue among bounded simply-connected planar domains. It is motivated by numerical evidence and by the expected tendency of optimal domains for magnetic eigenvalues to become more symmetric as the magnetic field grows; its resolution is not given here.

370343.title: Cavenagh–Hämäläinen–Lefevre–Stones completion conjecture for partial multi-Latin squares
370343.statement:
Let $r$ and $\lambda$ be positive integers. A **simple partial $\lambda$-Latin square** of order $r$ is an $r\times r$ array whose cells contain multisets of at most $\lambda$ symbols, with each symbol occurring at most $\lambda$ times in each row and column, and with no repeated symbol in any cell. A simple $\lambda$-Latin square of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array in which each cell contains a multiset of $\lambda$ symbols, each symbol occurs at most $\lambda$ times in each row and column, and no cell contains repeated symbols.

**Cavenagh–Hämäläinen–Lefevre–Stones' conjecture.** For each $r,\lambda\in\mathbb N$, there exists an integer $n(r,\lambda)$ such that, for every $n\geq n(r,\lambda)$, every simple partial $r\times r$ $\lambda$-Latin square can be extended to a simple $n\times n$ $\lambda$-Latin square.

The conjecture asks for a uniform sufficiently large order guaranteeing completion of every simple partial multi-Latin square. The paper states that it confirms this conjecture, while the supplied status for this candidate is open; the status should therefore be checked against the paper's final completion result.

370685.title: The four matroid polynomial conjectures
370685.statement:
Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a matroid, with Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathsf{M}}(x)$, $Z$-polynomial $Z_{\mathsf{M}}(x)$, inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial $Q_{\mathsf{M}}(x)$, and inverse $Z$-polynomial $Y_{\mathsf{M}}(x)$.

**The four matroid polynomial conjectures.** For every matroid $\mathsf{M}$, the polynomial $P_{\mathsf{M}}(x)$ is real-rooted, the polynomial $Z_{\mathsf{M}}(x)$ is real-rooted, the polynomial $Q_{\mathsf{M}}(x)$ has log-concave coefficients, and the polynomial $Y_{\mathsf{M}}(x)$ has log-concave coefficients.

The first, third, and fourth claims are supported primarily by computations for special families of matroids. For the second, $Z$-polynomials are known to be $\gamma$-positive, which is weaker than real-rootedness but stronger than unimodality; all four claims remain open here.

370825.title: Linear degree-count separation conjecture for super-minimally and uniformly connected graphs
370825.statement:
For an integer $k\geq 3$, let a graph be **super-minimally $k$-connected** if it is $k$-connected and no proper subgraph is $k$-connected. Let a graph be **uniformly $k$-connected** if every pair of distinct vertices is joined by exactly $k$ internally disjoint paths. A degree-$k$ vertex is a vertex of degree $k$.

**Linear degree-count separation conjecture.** There are constants $a_k$ and $b_k$ such that

$$
\text{every super-minimally } k\text{-connected graph has at least }a_k|V(G)|\text{ degree-}k\text{ vertices},
$$

$$
\text{every uniformly } k\text{-connected graph has at least }b_k|V(G)|\text{ degree-}k\text{ vertices},
$$

and

$$
\frac{k-1}{2k-1}<a_k<b_k.
$$

The case $k=3$ is verified in the paper by the stated lower bounds for super-minimally and uniformly $3$-connected graphs, while the conjecture remains open in general for $k\geq 4$.

371647.title: The gonality-tight graph conjecture
371647.statement:
Let $G$ be a gonality-tight graph with first gonality $k$ for some integer $k$, and let $g$ denote its genus. Write $K_G$ for the canonical divisor of $G$, and write $D\sim D'$ when two divisors are linearly equivalent. The $r$-th gonality is denoted by $\operatorname{gon}_r(G)$.

**Gonality-tight graph conjecture.** The following hold:

1. The genus of $G$ is

$$
g=\binom{k}{2}.
$$

2. The gonality sequence is

$$
\operatorname{gon}_r(G)=\begin{cases} l(k+1)-h & \text{if } r<g,\\ g+r & \text{if } r\geq g,\end{cases}
$$

where $1\leq l\leq k-2$ and $0\leq h\leq l$ are uniquely determined integers satisfying

$$
r=\frac{l(l+3)}{2}-h.
$$

3. If $D$ realizes the second gonality, then

$$
(k-2)\cdot D\sim K_G.
$$

Moreover, for every integer $1\leq l\leq k-2$, all divisors realizing the $\frac{l(l+3)}{2}$-th gonality are linearly equivalent to $l\cdot D$.

The conjecture is motivated by a large number of computational examples and predicts that gonality-tight graphs have a rigid genus, gonality sequence, and linear-equivalence structure for divisors realizing selected gonalities. Its status is not established by the supplied material.

375582.title: Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture for stable non-r-partite hypergraphs
375582.statement:
Fix $r\ge 2$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph, or **$r$-graph**, is a family of $r$-subsets of a vertex set; write $|\mathcal H|$ for its number of edges. For an $r$-graph $\mathcal F$, let

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal F)=\max\big\{|\mathcal H|:|V(\mathcal H)|=n\text{ and }\mathcal H\text{ is }\mathcal F\text{-free}\big\}.
$$

Assume that, for all sufficiently large $n$, the extremal $n$-vertex $\mathcal F$-free $r$-graph is unique, and denote it by $\operatorname{EX}(n,\mathcal F)$. Let $N_{\mathcal F}(\mathcal G)$ be the number of labelled copies of $\mathcal F$ in $\mathcal G$, and define

$$
c(n,\mathcal F)=\min\left\{N_{\mathcal F}(\operatorname{EX}(n,\mathcal F)\cup\{e\};e):e\in\binom{V(\operatorname{EX}(n,\mathcal F))}{r}\setminus\operatorname{EX}(n,\mathcal F)\right\}.
$$

**Mubayi's conjecture.** If $\mathcal F$ is a stable non-$r$-partite $r$-graph, then, for every positive integer $q$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $r$-graph with $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal F)+q$ edges contains at least

$$
q\,c(n,\mathcal F)
$$

copies of $\mathcal F$. This proposes that the one-edge cost above a rigid extremal construction gives the correct linear lower bound for every fixed excess $q$; the paper studies strong counterexamples, so the conjecture is not established here and its status should be checked.

375614.title: The odd square-plane conjecture for transversal difference numbers
375614.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, and set

$$
G_p=(\mathbb Z/p^2\mathbb Z)^2,\qquad H_p=pG_p.
$$

For a transversal $T$ of $G_p/H_p$, write $D(T)=T-T$ and let

$$
\delta(G_p,H_p)=\min_T |D(T)|.
$$

Every normalized transversal has the form $T_f=\{[x]+p[f(x)]:x\in\mathbb F_p^2\}$ for a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p^2$ with $f(0)=0$. For $u,x\in\mathbb F_p^2$, define

$$
c_u(x)=\frac{[x+u]-[x]-[u]}{p},\qquad d_u f(x)=f(x+u)-f(x)+c_u(x),
$$

and $A_u(f)=\{d_u f(x):x\in\mathbb F_p^2\}$.

**Odd square-plane conjecture.** For every odd prime $p$,

$$
\delta\bigl((\mathbb Z/p^2\mathbb Z)^2,p(\mathbb Z/p^2\mathbb Z)^2\bigr)=(2p-1)^2.
$$

Equivalently, for every function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p^2$,

$$
\sum_{u\in\mathbb F_p^2}|A_u(f)|\geq (2p-1)^2.
$$

The coordinate box attains $(2p-1)^2$. The paper proves the unconditional lower bound $3p^2-p-1$, leaving a gap of $(p-1)(p-2)$; small-prime computations, probabilistic arguments, and fixed-polynomial evidence support the conjecture, but arbitrary $p$-dependent liftings remain unresolved.

375815.title: Depth formula conjecture for squarefree powers of wheel edge ideals
375815.statement:
Let $\mathcal W_n$ be the wheel graph on $n+1$ vertices, let $I(\mathcal W_n)$ be its edge ideal in $R=\mathbbk[x_1,\ldots,x_n,v]$, and let $\nu(\mathcal W_n)$ denote its matching number. For integers $n\ge3$ and $1\le q\le\nu(\mathcal W_n)$, consider the $q$-th squarefree power $I(\mathcal W_n)^{[q]}$. **Depth conjecture for wheel squarefree powers.** For all such $n$ and $q$,

$$
\operatorname{depth}(R/I(\mathcal W_n)^{[q]})=2q-1,
$$

equivalently,

$$
\operatorname{pd}(R/I(\mathcal W_n)^{[q]})=n-2q+2.
$$

The conjecture is suggested by the complete computations reported for wheels with $5\le n\le9$ in the relevant low-power cases, together with the top-power cases for $n=5,\ldots,8$. It would give a uniform depth and projective-dimension formula throughout the full range of squarefree powers, beyond the computational evidence currently recorded.
